AGRICULTURE — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #6
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: AGRICULTURE
TIME ALLOWED: 120 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. How wet should a compost heap be? (1 mark)
   A. Dripping wet
   B. Damp like a squeezed sponge
   C. Covered by a pool of water
   D. Completely dry

2. What might happen if the water for a drip system is dirty? (1 mark)
   A. The holes may block
   B. The plants will grow faster
   C. The water will taste better
   D. The bucket will be lighter

3. What does mulch do? (1 mark)
   A. Keeps the soil moist by reducing evaporation
   B. Makes the soil hot
   C. Kills the plant
   D. Adds plastic to the soil

4. What could a school use to make a simple drip system? (1 mark)
   A. A stone
   B. A broom
   C. A plastic bottle with tiny holes in the cap
   D. A wooden door

5. What does it mean to conserve fuel? (1 mark)
   A. To burn as much as possible
   B. To hide it
   C. To use only what is needed and make it last
   D. To waste it

6. Why do children need an adult when cooking? (1 mark)
   A. Fuels and fire can burn people
   B. Adults always cook faster
   C. Fire is not dangerous
   D. Children cannot lift a spoon

7. Why is wet firewood a poor fuel? (1 mark)
   A. It makes a lot of smoke and gives little heat
   B. It lasts forever
   C. It has no smoke
   D. It burns very hot

8. What is thinning? (1 mark)
   A. Adding more seeds
   B. Making soil thin
   C. Removing extra seedlings so the rest have room
   D. Cutting all plants

9. What should be done first before pulling out seedlings when thinning? (1 mark)
   A. Cut the tops off
   B. Water the bed so the soil is soft
   C. Cover it with plastic
   D. Dry the bed

10. When should fruits be harvested? (1 mark)
   A. After they rot
   B. Before flowers appear
   C. When they are ripe
   D. While green and hard

11. Which is a woody tree fruit in this lesson? (1 mark)
   A. Grapes
   B. Tree tomato
   C. Raspberry
   D. Kiwi

12. Why is it best to plant fruit varieties that suit the local climate? (1 mark)
   A. They need no water
   B. They never get pests
   C. They grow and fruit better
   D. They cost more

13. Why does passion fruit need a trellis? (1 mark)
   A. Its stem is soft and cannot stand alone
   B. It grows underground
   C. It eats insects
   D. It is a tree

14. Where should you buy fruit seedlings? (1 mark)
   A. A trusted nursery or agrovet
   B. From a scrap yard
   C. From a stream
   D. From anyone on the road

15. Which group of animals is called poultry? (1 mark)
   A. Sheep and goats
   B. Zebras and giraffes
   C. Chickens, ducks and turkeys
   D. Cows and bulls

16. What is the young one of a goat called? (1 mark)
   A. Lamb
   B. Calf
   C. Kid
   D. Chick

17. Which domestic animal is often kept in dry areas for milk and meat? (1 mark)
   A. Duck
   B. Rabbit
   C. Camel
   D. Pig

18. Which of these is an indigenous chicken called in Kenya? (1 mark)
   A. Broiler
   B. Turkey
   C. Layer only
   D. Kienyeji

19. Why should we not skip breakfast? (1 mark)
   A. The body needs energy and nutrients to start the day
   B. Breakfast is a waste of money
   C. It makes you tired
   D. It is not real food

20. Which group does githeri belong to mainly? (1 mark)
   A. Drinks
   B. Only water
   C. Energy and body-building
   D. Only protective

21. Which meal is missing body-building foods? (1 mark)
   A. Ugali and sukuma wiki only
   B. Chapati, egg and tomato
   C. Rice, beans and cabbage
   D. Ugali, fish and spinach

22. Which of these is an energy-giving fat? (1 mark)
   A. Spinach
   B. Beans
   C. Oranges
   D. Cooking oil

23. Which food group gives the body energy? (1 mark)
   A. Protective foods only
   B. Water only
   C. Energy-giving foods
   D. Salt

24. How much oil is used for shallow frying? (1 mark)
   A. A small amount that covers the bottom of the pan
   B. A whole bottle
   C. None
   D. A full pot

25. What is the first thing to do with leftover cooked food? (1 mark)
   A. Leave it on the floor
   B. Cover it and store it safely
   C. Throw it in the road
   D. Leave it in the sun

26. Why is it a good idea to use the water from boiled vegetables in soup? (1 mark)
   A. It is poisonous
   B. It is dirty
   C. It contains vitamins that came out of the vegetables
   D. It has no use

27. Who should be with a child who is cooking? (1 mark)
   A. Nobody
   B. An adult
   C. A friend only
   D. A younger child

28. Which PPE would you wear on your hands to handle dirty things? (1 mark)
   A. Gloves
   B. Headgear
   C. Gumboots
   D. Dust mask

29. Should you share a toothbrush? (1 mark)
   A. No
   B. Yes with family
   C. Yes with friends
   D. Only at school

30. Which food is bad for teeth if eaten too often? (1 mark)
   A. Eggs
   B. Water
   C. Sweets
   D. Vegetables

31. Which PPE protects the nose and mouth from dust? (1 mark)
   A. Overall
   B. Dust mask
   C. Gumboots
   D. Gloves

32. What should you do after mopping a floor? (1 mark)
   A. Sweep it
   B. Put up a sign that the floor is wet
   C. Pour more water
   D. Run on it

33. Why should a rubbish bin have a lid? (1 mark)
   A. To make it heavy
   B. To keep out flies and rats
   C. To stop rubbish from rotting
   D. To look pretty

34. Which is recycling? (1 mark)
   A. Burning it
   B. Sending it to sea
   C. Burying it
   D. Turning used material into something new

35. Which waste should not be burnt because the smoke is harmful? (1 mark)
   A. Wood
   B. Paper
   C. Plastic
   D. Dry leaves

36. What is a pin cushion used for? (1 mark)
   A. Ironing cloth
   B. Measuring cloth
   C. Keeping needles and pins safe
   D. Cutting cloth

37. How should you hold the cloth if you are right-handed? (1 mark)
   A. In your teeth
   B. In the left hand while sewing with the right
   C. Under your foot
   D. Above your head

38. Why should you tie a knot in the thread before tacking? (1 mark)
   A. So that the thread stays in the cloth
   B. To make the thread thicker
   C. To make the cloth stiffer
   D. So the needle does not move

39. When is long and short tacking a good choice? (1 mark)
   A. It is never used
   B. For hems on very slippery cloth
   C. For curves only
   D. For long straight seams where a quick hold is enough

40. Which cloth is easiest for beginners? (1 mark)
   A. Slippery silk
   B. Thick leather
   C. Cotton
   D. Wire mesh

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
41. State two safety rules when making a scarecrow. (2 marks)

42. Describe how a group can share the work of growing a fruit tree at school. (4 marks)

43. How should cloth items such as overalls and cloth masks be cleaned? (3 marks)

44. Explain four ways germs can enter the body. (4 marks)

45. State three dangers of using fuels at home and how to avoid one of them. (3 marks)

46. Give three good personal hygiene practices apart from washing hands. (3 marks)

47. Why do some fruit trees take longer to give fruit than others? (3 marks)

48. Why should you brush teeth twice a day? (2 marks)

49. Why is tacking better than pins alone? (2 marks)

50. Describe how to plant a fruit seedling. (4 marks)

51. Plan a weekly cleaning schedule for the classroom using dusting, sweeping, mopping and refuse disposal. (5 marks)

52. Why must fish be dried before shallow frying? (3 marks)

53. Name three improvised cleaning tools and what each is made from. (3 marks)

54. Name three foods that can be shallow fried. (3 marks)

55. Explain how PPE should be stored and why. (4 marks)

56. Name three PPE items and what each protects. (3 marks)

57. Explain pruning. (2 marks)

58. Write a plan for growing a passion fruit plant from planting to harvest. (5 marks)

59. Explain what drip irrigation is. (2 marks)
pages.answers:
AGRICULTURE — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #6 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. B — Damp like a squeezed sponge
   Too dry stops rotting and too wet makes the heap smell sour.

2. A — The holes may block
   Dirt gets stuck in tiny holes.

3. A — Keeps the soil moist by reducing evaporation
   A covering of dry grass slows down drying of the soil.

4. C — A plastic bottle with tiny holes in the cap
   A bottle with small holes in its cap drips slowly.

5. C — To use only what is needed and make it last
   Conserving fuel means saving it.

6. A — Fuels and fire can burn people
   Adults can guide and help prevent accidents.

7. A — It makes a lot of smoke and gives little heat
   Wet wood wastes heat drying itself.

8. C — Removing extra seedlings so the rest have room
   Thinning gives strong plants space.

9. B — Water the bed so the soil is soft
   Wet soil lets you pull gently without harming others.

10. C — When they are ripe
   Ripe fruit is tastiest and has the most vitamins.

11. B — Tree tomato
   Tree tomato and guava are woody.

12. C — They grow and fruit better
   Wrong climate gives poor growth.

13. A — Its stem is soft and cannot stand alone
   Climbers need supports.

14. A — A trusted nursery or agrovet
   Good seedlings are disease-free and true to type.

15. C — Chickens, ducks and turkeys
   Poultry means birds kept for eggs and meat.

16. C — Kid
   A young goat is a kid.

17. C — Camel
   Camels survive in dry regions.

18. D — Kienyeji
   Kienyeji chickens are local breeds.

19. A — The body needs energy and nutrients to start the day
   Breakfast gives energy for school.

20. C — Energy and body-building
   Maize gives energy, beans give protein.

21. A — Ugali and sukuma wiki only
   Ugali and kale give energy and vitamins but no protein food.

22. D — Cooking oil
   Oils give a lot of energy.

23. C — Energy-giving foods
   Carbohydrates and fats give energy.

24. A — A small amount that covers the bottom of the pan
   Shallow frying uses a thin layer.

25. B — Cover it and store it safely
   Covered food stays safe from flies.

26. C — It contains vitamins that came out of the vegetables
   Some vitamins go into the cooking water.

27. B — An adult
   An adult helps prevent accidents.

28. A — Gloves
   Gloves cover the hands.

29. A — No
   Toothbrushes carry germs.

30. C — Sweets
   Sugar helps decay.

31. B — Dust mask
   A dust mask covers the nose and mouth.

32. B — Put up a sign that the floor is wet
   Wet floors are slippery.

33. B — To keep out flies and rats
   Lids stop pests.

34. D — Turning used material into something new
   Recycling reuses materials.

35. C — Plastic
   Burning plastics gives harmful smoke.

36. C — Keeping needles and pins safe
   It holds sharp objects.

37. B — In the left hand while sewing with the right
   This is the usual way.

38. A — So that the thread stays in the cloth
   A knot stops the thread pulling through.

39. D — For long straight seams where a quick hold is enough
   It is quicker.

40. C — Cotton
   Cotton is easy to handle.

SECTION B
----
41. (2 marks)
   Answer: Ask an adult to help with sharp or heavy work; do not use wire or broken glass; wear gloves for rough poles (any two).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each rule.

42. (4 marks)
   Answer: Make a chart with jobs such as watering, weeding, mulching and recording; take turns each week; check the plant daily; record dates of flowers and fruits.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct activity or arrangement.

43. (3 marks)
   Answer: Wash with soap and water, rinse well and dry in the sun to help kill germs.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each part.

44. (4 marks)
   Answer: Through the mouth from dirty hands, dirty food, dirty water, and through cuts or feet without shoes.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each way.

45. (3 marks)
   Answer: Fire burns, charcoal fumes are poisonous and gas can leak. Avoid one by keeping children away from fire, cooking in a place with fresh air or closing the gas valve after use.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for dangers, 1 mark for a correct way to avoid one.

46. (3 marks)
   Answer: Bathing daily, brushing teeth twice a day, keeping nails short, wearing clean clothes, drinking safe water (any three).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

47. (3 marks)
   Answer: Big trees such as mango grow slowly and need years before flowering, while pawpaw and passion fruit are small plants that fruit within about a year.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each for slow trees, fast plants, and reason of size or type.

48. (2 marks)
   Answer: It removes food and germs that cause decay and keeps the mouth fresh.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for removing food, 1 mark for preventing decay.

49. (2 marks)
   Answer: Pins can slip or prick, tacking holds cloth firmly.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

50. (4 marks)
   Answer: Water the seedling; remove the bag carefully; place at the same depth in the hole; fill with soil and firm; water and mulch.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each for four correct steps.

51. (5 marks)
   Answer: A table of days with jobs for each learner group: Monday dusting, Tuesday sweeping, Wednesday mopping, and refuse disposal each day, with tools and safety measures.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for jobs, 1 for tools, 1 for safety, 1 for fairness of sharing.

52. (3 marks)
   Answer: Wet food makes the hot oil splash, which can burn people, so the fish should be dried with a cloth.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for splash, 1 for burns, 1 for drying.

53. (3 marks)
   Answer: Duster from old cloth; mop from strips of cloth on a stick; dustpan from a cut jerrican.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each tool with material.

54. (3 marks)
   Answer: Eggs, fish, sausages, onions, chapati (any three).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each food.

55. (4 marks)
   Answer: Clean and dry, in a cupboard, rack or clean box, so it does not grow mould or spread germs, and labelled so it is used by the owner.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for storing, 2 marks for reasons.

56. (3 marks)
   Answer: Gloves protect hands; gumboots protect feet from mud; dust mask protects the nose and mouth from dust.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each item with its use.

57. (2 marks)
   Answer: It is cutting off dead, weak or crossing branches so that light and air can reach the plant.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for cutting, 1 mark for the purpose.

58. (5 marks)
   Answer: Build a trellis; dig and prepare a hole with compost; plant a seedling; water and mulch; tie the stem to the support; weed and prune; harvest ripe fruits and wash before eating.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct stage, up to 5.

59. (2 marks)
   Answer: It is watering plants slowly, drop by drop, next to their roots.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for slowly or drop by drop, 1 mark for near the roots.
